fixed: UX-PR79-01: wrap-anywhere is gone from every <td>/<th> this PR gave it. Long values (paths, keys, traces, references, plan keys, invoice numbers, UUIDs, names) now sit in an inner block, `block min-w-32 wrap-anywhere`. Emails sit in `min-w-40`. Sentence cells take no class at all: contracts/review.tsx terms, contracts/page.tsx Note (rendered through WholeDates), models/display.tsx quote, uploads/[documentId] error text, and the reports Table's Pattern. The reports Table's `wraps` prop is removed (both uses were the Pattern sentence), and its figure cells are now nowrap (components/reports/display.tsx:139-150). Sites include console/compliance:166,220-229, console/models:107, console/organizations/[id]:147,217,288,291,357, console/prospects:69, console/rule-releases:186, console/screening:100, console/terms:52, console/tickets:63,75, support:78, abstraction:116, abstraction/ledger:75, anomalies:76, cases:279, claims:164, contracts:116, contracts/[contractId]:87,96, coverage:262, mapping:127, mapping/[planId]:225, p/page.tsx:455, reconciliation:129-133, remittances:98, remittances/[id]:126,173, reports:259,322, roi:93, access-log:64,75, settings/agreements:110, uploads/[documentId]:195, settings/billing/[org]:150, models/display:125, pricing/display:566,576, template-mapper:192, releases/note:68 and reports/documents:127,307. Measured in the real build, these floors pushed three tables past their card, so each was fixed differently. (a) contracts/review.tsx:254-275: the approval now sits under the terms in the same cell (`div min-w-32 wrap-anywhere data-approval`), so the rate record's Fields table is two columns and fits both its half-width card at 1280 and a 390 px phone. A floored third column overflowed both. (b) claims/page.tsx:164: the patient name is plain words, and the claim control numbers (up to 50 characters) are a `min-w-32 wrap-anywhere` div. With the reviewer's min-w-40 the table was 910 px in an 893 px card at 1263 px. (c) packets/display.tsx:118-160: the line-schedule claim cell has no wrap-anywhere. The Placeholder component now also allows a break after `{{`, so it breaks only at `{{`, `_` and `:`. With an 8rem floor the table was 970 px in a 910 px card. layout-1280 now passes at both 1280 and 1263 px. Cases: the Deadline component (triage/display.tsx:46-56) gets flex-wrap so its status can drop under the date. Measured min-content went from 928 to 842 px (the table's min-w is 864 px). Prospects (console/prospects:69-125): Contact uses min-w-32 because its email is text-xs, Payers takes nothing (names), and the decline select is wrapped in `contain-inline-size`. Measured min-content went from 996 to 861 px.

UX-PR79-02: Dates and counts are now whitespace-nowrap in every table this PR changed. A date-time renders through a new `UtcTime` component (apps/web/src/components/dates.tsx) as two whole spans, so it can wrap between date and time but never inside either; the text is unchanged. Words that contain dates render through a new `WholeDates` component: contract windows, the calendar note, the content-due status and MappingText. Sites named by the reviewer: the Deadline date span (triage/display.tsx:52), cases Lines (cases/page.tsx:268), the anomalies service-date link cell (anomalies/page.tsx:80), billing Issued (settings/billing/[org]/page.tsx:163) and prospects Received (UtcTime). Every other date or count cell in the changed tables got the same treatment: console billing, compliance, the organizations list and detail, rule-releases, screening, terms, tickets, support, the abstraction page and its ledger, the packet page's Versions table, contracts, contracts/[contractId], mapping, mapping/[planId], packet-reviews, reconciliation, releases, the remittance detail, reports, roi, access-log, settings/agreements, template-mapper, releases/note, reports/documents, reports/roi.tsx and content-due.tsx. New unit test: components/dates.test.tsx. content-due.test.tsx:73 is updated for the new span.

proposals: SelectField (components/field.tsx, not a file of this PR) sets a table column to the width of its longest option, because `max-w-full` does not make a select compressible in automatic table layout; adding `w-full` does. Either add `w-full` to its select app-wide, or keep the `contain-inline-size` wrapper wherever a select sits in a table cell (as on console/prospects).

Hashes are still shortened to 12 characters and an ellipsis in places outside this PR's tables: cases/[caseId]/submissions/page.tsx:333, the packet page's document label (packet/page.tsx:47), pricing-runs/page.tsx:63, lib/cases/timeline.ts:73 and lib/pricing/causes.ts:67. None is hover-only, but the baseline asks for whole hashes. Proposed for a follow-up UX PR.

Use components/dates.tsx (UtcTime, WholeDates) for dates in prose and headings across the app, not only in tables, for example the proposal card title, the status pages and 'Last confirmed …'. Also consider a `<time dateTime>` element inside UtcTime.

The Hash component (packets/display.tsx) uses break-all, which lowers a table column's min-content the same way wrap-anywhere does. Give it a floored block variant for table cells, or have fix-1's unfloored-wrap rule also cover break-all (`break-all` / `word-break:break-all`).

Ticket and support subjects and messages, and ledger reasons, are floored with wrap-anywhere rather than left bare. Unlike plain product sentences, they are free text a person typed, and a pasted URL would otherwise widen the table without limit. Record this rule in the UX reviewer's checklist next to 'never cut to a hover title' (design P9).

fixed: F1: in apps/web/src/app/brand.css, a new rule `.pw-scroll-frame > [data-scroller] :focus-visible { outline-offset: -2px; --tw-ring-inset: inset; }` sits after the scroll-padding rule. A link or control inside a scroller now draws its outline inside its own box, and a Tailwind ring (field.tsx, ActionForm's refusal hand-off) is inset the same way, so the scroller no longer clips it. This goes past the reviewer's fix, which covered outlines only; I added the ring line so focus rings drawn with box-shadow are not clipped either. Checked in a Chromium harness running the real component and the CSS Tailwind builds: first and last links draw 'solid 2px', offset -2px, inside the scroller, and an input's ring computes to '2px inset'. The F4 browser step asserts it too.

F3: stacked-rows.tsx, the <ul> now has role="list" (the reason is in the StackedRows doc comment). The repo has no jsx-a11y plugin, so no lint disable was needed. stacked-rows.test.tsx pins at the old :86, :90, :219 and :229 now expect it.

F4: tables-phone.spec.ts gains cueByKeyboard(page, 'Cases'), run right after the cases route at 390 px. Tab reaches the 'Cases, scrolls sideways' region (tabTo in a11y.ts now accepts role 'region' and reads the frame's outline). The frame's outline is 'solid 2px'. At the start only data-edge-end is set and the fades are ::before 0 / ::after 1. ArrowRight scrolls the region and both edges fade. At the end only the start edge fades. Tab then moves to the first link, which shows 'solid 2px -2px' in the frame's colour, inside the scroller's box (this also proves F1). Passed in the final run.

N1: brand.css, `[data-slot="scroll-table"] > .pw-scroll-frame:dir(rtl)::before/::after` reverse the two gradients. The rule is scoped to the table holder so the text box's top and bottom fades are untouched. Tailwind keeps :dir(rtl) as written. Harness: in RTL, before is 'to left', after is 'to right', and the box's fades are unchanged.

N2: scroll-table.tsx useScroller keeps the scroller element in state, and the effect runs on [axis, element]. The DR-06 check of document.activeElement moved into the stable ref callback, because once the element was state, react-hooks/set-state-in-effect flagged the old in-effect setState. Harness, with React 19 StrictMode hydrating server markup: switching ScrollBox `as` from pre to div measures the new element (overflows, region, tab stop) and switching back gives 'fits'. DR-06 still holds: a server region focused before hydration keeps its tab stop and drops it after Tab. No console errors.

N3: stacked-rows.tsx has an exported rendersNothing(node): undefined, null, a boolean, '' or a list of those. An actions box renders only when it returns false. A new test covers false, '', [], [false, null], undefined, null and true (no box) and 0, text and a list of one element (box).

tables.test.ts, repeated-label rule: a cross-file analysis (labelFacts plus repeatedLabels). It follows a ScrollTable label through component props (destructured, renamed, defaults and props.x), constants, String(), templates, `+`/`??`/`||`, conditionals and relative imports. It flags a label that is the same in every row: inside a .map, .flatMap or Array.from callback, in a component or helper rendered from one (including `rows.map(Component)`), or a props-only label inside a component's own .map. Run against the PR head it flags exactly reconciliation:211 and abstraction/ledger:145 (F2), plus packets/pricing.tsx:81 (Lines not on current pricing, once per submission), which the reviewer missed. Fixer 2 has fixed all three. 13 self-test cases.

tables.test.ts, wrap rules: 'wrap-in-cell' fails on wrap-anywhere (or a variant of it) on a <td> or <th>. 'unfloored-wrap' fails when wrap-anywhere sits inside a cell on an element that neither has, nor sits inside, a block with a base min-w above zero; an inline span's min-w does not count. Class names are read through className strings, cn() calls and constants. 14 self-test cases. The first test now checks only the original table rules (TABLE_RULES), and each new rule has its own test.

tabTo in a11y.ts treats focus as visible if outlineStyle or boxShadow is set; it does not check the ring is unclipped. A geometric check that the focused box lies inside every clipping ancestor would catch F1-class defects on every route; today F4's step checks it on the Cases table only. It changes a helper many specs use, so it needs a full e2e run.

expectAccessible (desktop width) could also turn on landmark-unique. At 1280 px fitting tables are not regions, but cards and sections can still repeat names. A full-suite discovery run like this PR's at 390 px would show the cost first.
